translation: (Voiceover): Moonlight upon the clouds.. moonlight of the mogili flowers.. even when autumn sheds the leaves.. are you the spring that sprouts again; even when reduced to bare stumps.. are you the forest that puts out new shoots; are you the music of the waterfall.. oh.. the song of the wild mountain wind.. hoy...

Verse 1: Pitter-patter, pitter-patter the raindrops fall on the ploughed fields, splish-splash, splish-splash the floodwaters run; drip by drip, drip by drip the drizzle pours down; the chill of the soaking rains, and the torment of flies and mosquitoes - the chill of the soaking rains, and the torment of flies and mosquitoes; on the day there is no work, the hungry belly burns with fasting - on the day there is no work, the hungry belly burns with fasting; the adivasi's life is one cut off from play and from the hunt - the adivasi's life is one cut off from play and from the hunt; even when work and songs grow scarce, the pain of starvation deaths remains - even when work and songs grow scarce, the pain of starvation deaths remains; it is a horror, a crime, a horror, a crime - the forest wails and weeps.. the forest wails and weeps.. pitter-patter, pitter-patter the raindrops fall, splish-splash, splish-splash the floodwaters run

Verse 2: Those living along the ravine went looking for help, and found only more want keeping them company - found only more want keeping them company; when they borrowed at interest to plant cotton, the compounding interest left them with nothing - left them with nothing; the money earned from plucking leaf and wild honey went straight to paying off the shrine's dues - went to paying off the shrine's dues; once the railway line took hold, the land itself changed hands - the land changed hands; it is a horror, a crime, a horror, a crime - the forest wails and weeps.. the forest wails and weeps.. pitter-patter, pitter-patter the raindrops fall, splish-splash, splish-splash the floodwaters run

Verse 3: The timber went to the company, the land went to the trader Pappu Bhai - the timber went to the company, the land went to the trader Pappu Bhai; the hamlet ended up sunk beneath the canal, with no shelter left standing - no shelter left standing; there is no education, no job, not even a guarantee of what little remains - no education, no job, not even a guarantee; when those who ask come forward, those who beat them fall upon them - those who beat them fall upon them; it is a horror, a crime, a horror, a crime - the forest wails and weeps.. the forest wails and weeps.. pitter-patter, pitter-patter the raindrops fall, splish-splash, splish-splash the floodwaters run

Verse 4: The town drove us out, the forest hemmed us in - the town drove us out, the forest hemmed us in; the self-rule handed down since our grandfathers' time has been shackled and seized - shackled and seized; a token, eyewash reservation brings nothing to our feet, nothing to our stomachs - brings nothing to our feet, nothing to our stomachs; in this age of corrupt vote-politics, self-rule in our own village never comes - self-rule in our own village never comes; it is a horror, a crime, a horror, a crime - the forest wails and weeps.. the forest wails and weeps.. pitter-patter, pitter-patter the raindrops fall, splish-splash, splish-splash the floodwaters run

Verse 5: Throughout history the adivasis' uprisings have gone on and on - throughout history the uprisings have gone on and on; demanding self-rule, wanting to govern ourselves - demanding self-rule, wanting to govern ourselves; the beat of the tudum drum rang out anew, the war-conch and horn resounded - the war-conch and horn resounded; the peacock danced with tail spread wide, mother forest thrilled with joy - mother forest thrilled with joy; roaring, roaring, the thunder of clouds roars, the forest is filled with the lion's roar.. the forest is filled with the lion's roar.. in nature's lap the birds chirp kilakila kilakila, the frogs croak bekabeka bekabeka, the koel sings kuhu kuhu - this is rela music.. our dolu-drum music.. the forest's own music.. the song of the people's liberation.. rela music, our dolu-drum music, the forest's music, the song of the people's liberation, rela rela rela re... rela rela rela re...
summaryEn: Marked as a Tribal Protest song from the 2023 album 'Vimalakka Hits', this piece opens with a lyrical voiceover comparing endurance through hardship to a forest that always sprouts again after autumn, before moving into five verses that catalogue the everyday suffering of adivasi (tribal, forest-dwelling) communities. Each verse pairs vivid nature imagery of rain and floods with a specific grievance: hunger on jobless days, debt from cotton grown on borrowed money, honey and forest produce earnings swallowed by shrine dues, land and timber seized by companies and traders, displacement by canals and railway lines, denial of education and jobs, and reservation policy dismissed as a hollow gesture that changes nothing in practice. A refrain - 'it is a horror, a crime, the forest wails and weeps' - closes each verse like a protest chant. The final verse turns from lament to defiance, invoking the long history of adivasi uprisings and the demand for self-rule, and ends with an exuberant burst of forest sounds - birds, frogs, the koel, drums - reframed as 'the song of the people's liberation,' turning natural imagery into a symbol of resistance and hope.
summaryTe: 2023లో వచ్చిన 'వైమలక్క హిట్స్' ఆల్బమ్‌లోని ఈ గిరిజన నిరసన గీతం, శరదృతువు తర్వాత ఎప్పుడూ మళ్ళీ చిగురించే అడవితో కష్టాలను తట్టుకునే ఓర్పును పోల్చుతూ ఒక కవితాత్మక వాయిస్ ఓవర్‌తో మొదలవుతుంది. తర్వాత ఐదు చరణాల్లో ఆదివాసీ (అటవీ) సమాజాల నిత్య బాధలను వర్ణిస్తుంది. ప్రతి చరణం వర్షం, వరదల ప్రకృతి చిత్రాలను ఒక నిర్దిష్ట ఫిర్యాదుతో జతచేస్తుంది - పని లేని రోజుల్లో ఆకలి, అప్పు తెచ్చి పత్తి వేస్తే వడ్డీ మోతతో నష్టం, తేనె అటవీ ఉత్పత్తుల ఆదాయం దేవర కొలువుకు హరించుకుపోవడం, కంపెనీలు వ్యాపారులు భూమి కర్రను లాక్కోవడం, కాలువలు రైల్వే లైన్ల వల్ల నిర్వాసితం కావడం, చదువు ఉద్యోగం లేకపోవడం, రిజర్వేషన్ కేవలం కంటి తుడుపుగా మిగలడం. ప్రతి చరణం చివర 'ఘోరం నేరం, అడవి గొల్లుమని ఏడ్చేరా' అనే పల్లవి ఒక నిరసన నినాదంలా వస్తుంది. చివరి చరణం విలాపం నుండి ధిక్కారానికి మారి, ఆదివాసుల సుదీర్ఘ తిరుగుబాట్ల చరిత్రను, స్వయం పాలన డిమాండ్‌ను ప్రస్తావిస్తుంది, చివరగా పక్షులు, కప్పలు, కోకిల, డోలు శబ్దాలతో నిండిన ఉత్సాహభరిత ముగింపుతో వీటిని 'జన విముక్తి గీతం'గా మలుస్తూ ప్రకృతి చిత్రాలను ప్రతిఘటన, ఆశ చిహ్నాలుగా మారుస్తుంది.
